extracted.intended_audience: Prospective ONR applicants preparing grant, cooperative agreement, or TIA proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a technical proposal and required forms in response to the ONR BAA (N00014-22-S-B001), including technical narrative, budget, data management plan, certifications, and administrative registrations. Covers proposal content, budget justification, submission procedures, and compliance/certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental compliance / NEPA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the applicant will ensure compliance with environmental statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies and recipients must comply with environmental planning/regulatory requirements (e.g., NEPA). If awards constitute "major Federal actions" (40 C.F.R 1508.1(q)) agencies may need to prepare NEPA documentation such as an EIS, even if only providing grant funds. Most ONR-funded field research is covered by a NEPA categorical exclusion (especially lab research that complies with other safety/environmental/natural resource laws). Questions should be referred to the technical point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 7 – Project Summary/Abstract handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave Field 7 blank; complete Form SF424, Project Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error message occurs when leaving Block 7 blank, upload the Project Abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 8 – Project Narrative / Technical Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe clearly the research, including the objective and approach to be performed, keeping in mind the evaluation criteria. Attach the entire proposal narrative to R&R Other Project Information form in Field 8 as a single PDF file saved as 'Technical Proposal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technical proposal must describe the research in sections (Cover Page, Table of Contents, Technical Approach, Future Naval Relevance, Project Schedule and Milestones, Reports). Typing a file name in the box is prohibited; use 'Add Attachment' to attach the single PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Proposal – Cover Page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Page must include the words 'Technical Proposal' and the following items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (a) BAA Number: N00014-22-S-B001; (b) Title of Proposal; (c) Identity of prime Offeror and complete list of subawards, if applicable; (d) Technical contact (name, address, phone/fax, email); (e) Administrative/business contact (name, address, phone/fax, email); (f) Proposed period of performance (identify both the base period and any options, if included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Proposal – Table of Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an alphabetical/numerical listing of the sections within the proposal, including corresponding page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scientific or technical concepts that will be investigated, providing the complete research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what is innovative about the proposed approach. Describe the proposed approach compared to alternate approaches other researchers have taken. Given a successful completion, describe the results, new knowledge, or insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future Naval Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe potential Naval relevance and contributions of the effort to the agency’s specific mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Schedule and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of the schedule of events and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports (deliverables expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify typical reports required under a research effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample reports typically required: Technical and Financial Progress Reports, Final Report. Note: Grants do not include the delivery of software, prototypes, and other hardware deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the overall management approach and provide rationale for participation of key team members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned relationships with any subawardees or collaborators. This is a single PI award; if there are subawardees/collaborators, explain how the proposed team fits the single PI structure. If appropriate, briefly describe anticipated schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the qualifications of the proposed Principal Investigator and any other key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offeror Responsibility information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information to assist ONR in evaluating the offeror's responsibility prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe: adequate resources or ability to obtain them; ability to comply with grant conditions considering existing/current commitments; performance history managing Federal awards and extent previously awarded amounts will be expended prior to future awards; record of integrity and business ethics; qualifications and eligibility to receive an award under applicable laws; organization, experience, accounting, operational controls and technical skills (or ability to obtain them), including property control systems, quality assurance measures, and safety programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document describing which data generated will be shared and preserved, how it will be done, or justification why sharing/preservation is not possible or appropriate. Limit: no more than 2 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss: types of data/software/other materials to be produced; how data will be acquired; time and location of acquisition if pertinent; how data will be processed; file formats and naming conventions; description of QA/QC measures during collection/analysis/processing; description of dataset origin when using existing data resources; description of standards for data and metadata format/content; appropriate timeframe for preservation; balance between value of preservation and associated cost/administrative burden with justification; statement that data cannot be made public when national security or controlled unclassified information concerns exist (example wording referencing DoD Directive 5230.09). See DoD Instruction 3200.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 9 – Bibliography & References
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload Bibliography/References Cited as a single PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 10 – Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities available for performing the proposed research and any additional facilities the applicant proposes to acquire at its own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate government-owned facilities already possessed that will be used. Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 11 – Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any equipment available or any additional equipment the application proposes to acquire at its own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate government-owned equipment that will be used. Justify the need for each equipment item. Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Budget – use of forms and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offeror must use Grants.gov forms (including SF Research and Related (R&R) Budget Form). If options are proposed, include pricing for option periods. Include a separate PDF providing justification/supporting documentation for each element of cost attached under Section K 'Budget Justification'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemized budget shall include specified categories and costs rounded to the nearest dollar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Direct Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Include individual labor categories or persons, with associated labor hours and unburdened direct labor rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide escalation rates for out years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Administrative and Clerical Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and clerical salaries are normally indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct charging may be appropriate when a major project requires extensive administrative/clerical support significantly greater than normal and routine levels. Budgets proposing direct charging must be supported with a budget justification describing the major project and the administrative/clerical work to be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Fringe Benefits and Indirect Costs (F&A/Overhead/G&A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the rates and calculation of the costs for each rate category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rates have been approved/negotiated by a Government agency, provide a copy of the memorandum/agreement. If the entity has never received a negotiated indirect cost rate, they may elect to charge a de minimis rate of 10% of modified total direct costs or provide sufficient detail to enable a determination of allowability/allocability/reasonableness and how rates are calculated. See 2 CFR 200.414(f). If composite rates are used, provide calculations used in deriving them. Additional information may be requested if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Travel
rubrics_metrics.description: For each proposed trip include purpose, origin and destination (if known), approximate duration, number of travelers, and estimated cost per trip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify estimates based on organization's historical average cost per trip or other reasonable basis. Estimates and resultant costs must conform to applicable Federal cost principles. Offerors may include travel costs for the Principal Investigator to attend peer reviews described in Section II of the BAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Subawards/Subcontracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description of work to be performed by subrecipients/subcontractors and submit detailed cost proposals for each subaward using the R&R budget form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same requirements apply to subawards as to prime categories. Proposal and supporting documentation must be received and reviewed before Government completes its cost analysis. Preferred method is to include subcontractor info with the Prime's proposal; alternatively it may be provided in a sealed envelope or emailed directly to the Program Officer at time of prime submission and must identify proposal title and prime Offeror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a breakdown of consultant hours, hourly rate, and any other proposed consultant costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copy of signed Consulting Agreement or other documentation supporting proposed consultant rate/cost, and a copy of the consultant’s proposed statement of work if not already separately identified in the prime contractor’s proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Materials & Supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all proposed materials and supplies including quantities, unit prices, and basis for estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis for estimate examples: quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Recipient Acquired Equipment or Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If acquisition of equipment/facilities is proposed, provide justification and an itemized list with basis for estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable items normally limited to research equipment not already available for the project. General purpose equipment (e.g., personal computers) should not be requested unless used primarily/exclusively for the project; include statement indicating how each item will be integrated into the program. Equipment/facilities are normally furnished by the Recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Other Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all proposed other direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Graduate Assistant tuition, laboratory fees, report and publication costs. Provide basis for estimate (quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget – Conference/Workshop Funding restrictions and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposal requests funds for hosting or attending a conference/workshop/symposium, include specific supporting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) ONR will not sponsor an ONR/Navy/DoD event — provide list of other sponsors and requested amounts. 2) Funds generally may not be used to pay for food or beverages as a direct cost except in exceptional circumstances; requires factual support and Grants Officer determination that expense is reasonable/allocable/allowable. 3) Specify how event/outcomes will directly/programmatically relate to US Naval or Marine Corps Science & Technology Plan, identify focus areas to be addressed, provide technical/scientific objectives and desired outcomes (e.g., proceedings, articles, algorithms, tools, additional research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee/Profit policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee/profit is unallowable under assistance agreements at either the prime or the subaward level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee/profit may be permitted on contracts issued by the prime awardee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect degree information and current/pending support for all senior/key personnel, including PI and Co-PIs, whether or not efforts are funded by DoD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Degree Type and Degree Year; Current and Pending Support must list Title and objectives; percentage per year devoted to other projects; total amount of support for each other project; name and address of agencies/other parties supporting other projects; period of performance. Upload biosketch/CV/resume to Biographical Sketch field. Additional senior/key persons can be added. Failure to include required information may cause application to be returned without further review; DoD reserves right to request further details before final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Personal Data (demographics form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the personal data form with name fields of PI and any Co-PIs completed; provision of demographic information is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demographic info (gender, race, ethnicity, disability) will be used for statistical purposes only and may be accessible to the reviewer but will not be considered in evaluation. Applicants may select 'Do not wish to provide' for any items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and application submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall submit applications online through Grants.gov and must register the organization and users appropriately before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must have a DUNS Number, active SAM registration, and Grants.gov account. Steps include: obtain DUNS, register with SAM, create Grants.gov account, add an organizational profile (entering DUNS), request and obtain roles (EBiz POC authorizes AOR role), track role status. Electronic signature: AOR role insertion into signature line; EBiz POC must authorize personnel with authority to make legally binding commitments. White Papers must NOT be submitted through Grants.gov (use FedConnect). All attachments must be PDF. Grants.gov Workspace may be used to create/complete/submit; create workspace, add participants, complete required forms, check for errors. Adobe Reader compatibility notes provided. Mandatory fields marked with asterisk. Complete SF-424 fields first as they propagate to other forms. Submit at least 48 hours prior to close date. Grants.gov provides a tracking number and acknowledgement email. Grants.gov applicant support phone/email provided for technical help; get ticket number for troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely Receipt and Proof of Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of timely submission is the official date/time stamp that Grants.gov generates when it receives the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant with the AOR role receives acknowledgement and Grants.gov Tracking Number (GRANTXXXXXXXX) and an email with official date/time stamp. ONR's acknowledgement upon retrieval is separate. Applications received by Grants.gov after the established due date are late and will not be considered. Applicants with slow internet should allow time for transmission and follow up with Grants.gov Support Center for errors/tickets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Qualifications (Grants Officer determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified for an award a potential recipient must meet standards at 32 CFR 22.415.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, a Grants Officer will award only to qualified recipients who: (1) have management capability and adequate financial and technical resources to execute the program given those provided by the award; (2) have a satisfactory record of executing such programs/activities (if a prior recipient); (3) have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; and (4) be otherwise qualified and eligible to receive an award under applicable laws/regulations. Applicants are requested to provide info with proposal submissions to assist Grants Officer's evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS (integrity/performance information) review
rubrics_metrics.description: For Federal awards with total Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, the agency will review and consider information about the applicant in FAPIIS (designated integrity system accessible through SAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may review and comment on information about themselves in the system. The Federal awarding agency will consider applicant comments along with other information when assessing applicant risk per 2 CFR 200.206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide information describing processes/systems in place to comply with reporting requirements on subawards and executive total compensation as codified in 2 CFR Part 170.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception/exemption applies. Refer to 2 CFR Part 170 (including Appendix A) for details on requirements, exceptions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certification (SF 424 (R&R) supplements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities must attest they will abide by requirements of various laws/regulations and supplemental sections; submit required documentation such as SF-LLL and disclosures as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation is an attestation that the entity will abide by laws/regulations and supplemental statements in Section F.2.iv above. Applicants must submit documentation including SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities if applicable, and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or felony conviction under Federal law as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Restrictions on Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: For grants/cooperative agreements/TIAs greater than $100,000 applicants must certify compliance with lobbying restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification states no Federal appropriated funds have/will be paid to influence agency personnel or Members of Congress in connection with award. If non-Federal funds were/will be paid for lobbying, applicant must complete SF-LLL. Applicant must require inclusion of this certification language in award documents for all subawards at all tiers. Submission is a material representation of fact under 31 U.S.C. 1352; failure to file required certification may lead to civil penalties of $10,000–$100,000 per failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Prohibition on Using Funds with Entities that Require Certain Internal Confidentiality Agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17, applicant certifies it does not require employees/contractors/subrecipients to sign internal confidentiality agreements that would prohibit or restrict reporting fraud, waste, or abuse to authorized Federal investigative/law enforcement representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a supplement to the SF424 (R&R) financial assistance certifications and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Disclosure of Funding Sources (NDAA Section 223(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17, applicant certifies compliance with Section 223(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA FY2021 regarding disclosure of current and pending support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires (a) PI and other key personnel certify current and pending support is current/accurate/complete; (b) agree to update disclosure at agency request prior to award and during the award term as appropriate; (c) PI and key personnel have been made aware of requirements. False statements may subject individuals to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest – Codes of Conduct and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c) Codes of Conduct to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in award/admin of contracts supported by federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General requirement: disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest for the applicant and any identified subrecipient. ONR may request additional information and may ask for a conflict of interest mitigation plan after submission; mitigation plan is subject to ONR approval. (Text continues with Scientific Conflict of Interest subsection.)
